content: Benznidazole is indicated for the treatment of Chagas disease (American trypanosomiasis) caused by Trypanosoma cruzi in children aged 2 to 12 years. Its safety and efficacy have not been established in children under 2 years of age. For children aged 2 to 12 years, the recommended dosage is 5 to 8 mg/kg/day, administered orally in two divided doses approximately 12 hours apart, for a duration of 60 days. The drug has not been evaluated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. This indication has been approved under accelerated approval based on the number of treated patients who became immunoglobulin G (IgG) antibody-negative against recombinant antigens of T. cruzi. Continued approval may depend on verification and description of clinical benefit in confirmatory trials. Benznidazole is contraindicated in patients who have taken disulfiram within the last two weeks due to the risk of increased toxicity caused by aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibition. Psychotic reactions have been reported in patients co-administered disulfiram and nitroimidazole agents, which are structurally related to benznidazole. Additionally, benznidazole increases the toxicity of ethanol through aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibition. Patients should avoid consuming alcoholic beverages or products containing propylene glycol during and for at least three days after completing benznidazole therapy. Symptoms such as abdominal cramps, nausea, vomiting, headaches, and flushing may occur if alcohol or propylene glycol-containing products are consumed during this period. Benznidazole may interact with certain immunosuppressive therapies, including axicabtagene ciloleucel, brexucabtagene autoleucel, ciltacabtagene autoleucel, idecabtagene vicleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, and tisagenlecleucel. These interactions can increase the immunosuppressive effects of both agents, raising the risk of infection. It is recommended to avoid or use alternative drugs in such cases. Due to the potential for serious adverse reactions and the risk of Chagas disease transmission, breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with benznidazole. Benznidazole is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. The drug is approximately 44-60% protein-bound, with an unknown metabolic pathway and a half-life of 13 hours (based on single-dose studies in healthy volunteers). It is excreted via urine and feces. Dosage is based on body weight, and the 100-mg tablets are scored to allow precise dosing by splitting into halves (50 mg) or quarters (25 mg). Benznidazole may be taken with or without food. The medication should be stored at controlled room temperature (20-25°C or 68-77°F), with permissible excursions to 15-30°C (59-86°F). The bottle should be tightly closed and protected from moisture. This information is provided for general informational and educational purposes. For the most current and specific formulary information, contact the applicable plan provider.
